name: Home engineer (structural inspections)

pf.license.need: A structural evaluation is engineering work: each engineer holds their own state professional engineer (PE) license, and the firm holds a firm certificate where the state asks for one. Only a licensed engineer evaluates alone, and only a licensed engineer seals a report or letter. An engineer-in-training works under a licensed engineer who reviews and seals.
pf.license.ask: Each engineer's license number, type and state. The firm's certificate number, where the state's form asks for one.
pf.license.who_holds: Each engineer holds their own license. The firm holds its own certificate where required. A seal goes only on work the sealing engineer did or directly supervised.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: Where the state requires licensed engineers: no evaluation is offered until the firm's and the engineer's numbers check out. A sealed letter is offered only with an engineer whose license is current.
pf.license.insurance_bond: Professional liability (errors-and-omissions) insurance where the state's form requires it. Shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word.
pf.license.shown_to_customers: The engineer's license number on offers, confirmations and the report, where the state's rules require it.
pf.license.drone: A roof viewed by drone: only by a pilot who meets the federal rules for flying for pay. The plug-in never offers a drone view unless Sam says his pilot qualifies.
pf.license.not_this_work: Repairs or construction of any kind, soil borings, mold or asbestos testing, and code enforcement. They are other businesses' work, never booked under the engineer's plug-in. A sealed letter for a building the engineer has not seen is never offered.

pf.services.pattern: Set service: one evaluation at the property, priced by the home's size, with a written report later.

list.money: card saved at booking; charged at DONE

pf.services.start_times: Set starts, like 8:30am and 1:00pm. The walk-through time is told at booking.
pf.services.notice: 2 days' notice by default, so access can be set up. A sooner time only if Sam says yes.
pf.services.capacity: One engineer per evaluation. Add-ons only with someone who does them.
pf.services.nobody_home: Yes: nobody needs to be at the property to start. The engineer gets in with a lockbox code the agents or the owner set up. The client is welcome at the walk-through.
pf.services.online: Consults, plan checks and second opinions can be done by video.
pf.services.not_offered: Repairs or construction, soil borings, mold or asbestos testing, code enforcement, appraisals, and an emergency shoring crew.
pf.services.partner_work: Repairs go to a contractor the customer picks. This business never names or refers one and takes no referral fee.

pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult: an owner, a buyer, or an agent or manager for their client. The client named on the agreement signs it. A tenant books only with the owner's yes on the access link. Nobody books an evaluation of a building they have no right to enter.

words: loud cracking or popping from the walls or floor right now
a floor, ceiling or wall giving way right now
what_happens: A gas smell, sparks, smoke or a carbon monoxide alarm: whoever is there gets out first, then calls 911 and the gas company from outside. No booking until the home is safe.

A floor, ceiling or wall giving way right now, or loud cracking from the structure: everyone gets out and stays out, then calls 911. No booking until the fire department or the building department says it is safe to go in. The engineer never enters a building that is moving.

Live wires hanging down or flooding up to the outlets: stay away from that area, and call 911 if anyone is in danger. The evaluation can be booked for the rest of the property; the engineer will not enter that area.
A slowly growing crack, a sloping floor or a sticking door is a normal reason to book, not an emergency. The booking goes on.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: No, for gas, sparks, smoke, a carbon monoxide alarm or a structure giving way right now. Yes, with the unsafe area left out, for live wires or flooding. Yes for everything else.

pf.first_steps.agreement: The business's own engineering agreement (what is and isn't evaluated, and how the report may be used), signed on the secure page before the time is booked. Rosie never writes or edits it.
pf.first_steps.access: Access set up by whoever controls the property: the owner or occupant, or a buyer's agent with the listing agent, on a link the client forwards. Due by 5pm the day before.
pf.first_steps.documents: Earlier reports, drawings, permits and photos the client has, added on the secure page if there are any.
pf.first_steps.deck: For a deck or balcony inspection: furniture, planters and grills cleared, and the space under the deck reachable.
prep_for_reminder: Water, power and gas on, with the pilot lights lit
Clear paths to the basement or crawl space, the attic hatch and the garage walls
Pets out of the house, or put away
Move boxes and shelves away from any wall or floor with a crack, where you can
For a deck: furniture, planters and grills cleared

pf.visit.check_in: Most evaluations start with nobody there: the engineer gets in with the lockbox code, and DONE confirms the visit. A client who meets the engineer gives the code at the door, or at the walk-through.
pf.visit.entry_codes: The lockbox code is shown only to the engineer, only on the day, and each view is logged.
pf.visit.what_is_checked: Foundation and slab, floors and framing, walls, roof framing and attic, chimney, porches and decks, and drainage next to the house. Cracks are measured and photographed; floor levels are read with a laser level.
pf.visit.not_examined: Anything that can't be reached or seen, like a finished basement wall or a flooded crawl space, is listed as not examined. A return visit is offered for the trip fee, with the client's OK.
pf.visit.walk_through: Main findings only, in plain words: no repair prices and no repair offers.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: An add-on (a floor elevation survey, crack gauges, a sealed letter) only if the client says yes first, priced before it is done. The fee never depends on what is found or on the sale closing.
pf.visit.proof_done: DONE from the engineer's phone, with photos. The report follows by the date promised.
pf.visit.report: A written report with photos, sent on a secure link by the date promised at booking. A sealed letter is added once the engineer has finished the review. Where the state's rules set a deadline, Rosie tracks it and reminds Sam before it passes.
pf.visit.report_release: Sam picks per service: the report goes out at once, or once the bill is paid. Where the state's rules forbid holding a report, it goes out at once. A sealed letter is never held back for a repair or for a sale.

pf.money.start: Evaluations: a card saved at booking, charged at DONE. Consults and plan checks at the office: a card saved for the fee, paid at the office after.
pf.money.other_ways: Nothing taken and the bill texted after; paid in full when booking (a follow-up visit); a deposit and the rest on the bill for a very large building quoted first.
pf.money.deposits: None by default on a set-price evaluation. A very large building quoted from photos may take a deposit; the cap, if any, comes from the state form.
pf.money.fees: Late cancel, or no way in at the start time: the business's own trip fee (the example: $89). A return visit when part of the building could not be reached: the trip fee. Sam confirms each one; no answer, no fee.
pf.money.fee_rule: The fee never depends on what the evaluation finds, on the sale closing, or on the repair that follows.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes engineering services, from the state form.

never_in_texts: The street address in a first text to someone new
Findings, photos of cracks and the report: only the secure link
pf.messages.who_gets_texts: The client. The agent or manager who sets up access only after their own yes on the access page.
pf.messages.minors: Nobody under 18 books or signs the agreement.

skills: Consults and plan checks at the office
pf.staff.licenses: Each engineer's own PE license, where the state licenses engineers. Only a licensed engineer evaluates alone or seals.
pf.staff.stand_in: Another engineer with the same license and skills may stand in, with the client's OK first.
pf.staff.supervision: An engineer-in-training works only with a licensed engineer who reviews and seals the work, where the state's rules allow it.
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes over $500 and every fee. Pat, the office manager, may too; Sam's answer wins.

pf.rules.agreement: A signed engineering agreement before the evaluation starts, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.seal: Only the licensed engineer who did or directly supervised the work seals a letter or report. Never sealed for a building the engineer has not seen.
pf.rules.report_deadline: The report reaches the client by the date promised at booking. A later date is told to the client before the old one passes. Rosie tracks the date.
pf.rules.fee_independence: The fee can't depend on what is found, on the sale closing, or on the repair that follows.
pf.rules.referral_fees: No referral fee to or from a contractor or an agent, where the state's rules bar it.
pf.rules.repair_ban: No repair or construction work at a home this firm evaluated, for the time the state's rules set. Sam can keep it as his own rule anywhere.
pf.rules.license_shown: The license number on offers, confirmations and the report, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, or longer where the state's rules ask: the agreement, the report, the photos and the measurements.

matter_most: The sale falls through: an ordinary cancel, judged only by the notice given.
Access isn't set up by 5pm the day before: Sam is asked to call, and the client is told. The booking stays.
The lockbox code doesn't work: the engineer texts it, the client and the access person get a link for a new code, and the walk-through moves.
Part of the building can't be reached: those areas are listed as not examined, and a return visit is offered for the trip fee.
The engineer sees a danger at the visit: everyone goes outside first, and 911 is given for anyone in danger.
The report runs late: the client hears the new date before the old one passes.
The client asks the firm to fix or build what it found: Rosie says this firm doesn't do repair work at a home it evaluated.
The client asks for a sealed letter: only after the engineer has seen the building.
The client asks the engineer to change the findings: the findings are the engineer's own; a factual mistake goes to Sam.
A moved evaluation carries the signed agreement and the access link to the new date.
pf.edges.rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes:
Kept words: 'Trip fee' (the $89 fee for a late cancel or no way in, the parent's word too), 'Grace' (the master's grace time), 'leak' and 'color' (the master's shared safety and fairness lines, S13-40 lists color among protected traits).
New profession on the REDESIGN 2 master (batch S1, Tue Oct 27 2026), started from the refitted inspector overlay (set 'from'): an engineer's structural evaluation runs like an inspection (a signed agreement before booking, access set up by whoever controls the property, a walk-through of the main findings, a written report later), so the inspector is the right parent.
Flow B is the usual side: Lee Home Engineering (structural evaluations of houses, condos and small multi-unit buildings, with deck and balcony inspections as the second kind of work). Flow A is Lee Engineering Office, Sam's office: a 20-minute quick consult, plan checks and second opinions, at the office, by video or at the property.
Prices are the example business's own: structural evaluation $495 (house up to 3,000 sq ft), foundation crack evaluation $395, deck and balcony inspection $350, follow-up visit after repairs $150 (paid in full), floor elevation survey $199 ($249 when Sam goes), crack gauges $160, sealed letter $150, a multi-unit building quoted from the listing and plans at $640 (Sam OKs over $500), trip fee $89. Flow A: quick consult $35, photo review $20, second opinion on a report $55, beam and wall-removal plan check $140, at the property $75.
Money, flow B: main list|card|card (a card saved at booking, charged at DONE), list|none|bill (the bill after; the report goes out once it is paid, Sam's setting), list|full|none (a follow-up visit paid in full when booking), photos|deposit|bill (a very large building quoted first: $160 deposit, $480 on the bill). Flow A: list|card|counter (main), list|none|counter, list|full|none, list|card|card (Saturday mornings with no front desk). No visit-priced path: the fee never depends on what the evaluation finds.
Only licensed engineers evaluate alone or seal. A sealed letter is offered only for a building the engineer has seen, and never held back for a repair or a sale. The firm does no repair work at a home it evaluated (a switch from the state's form, or Sam's own rule). These are generic switches in pf.rules: no state, city or law is named.
Danger words (pf.safety): a gas smell, sparks or smoke, a carbon monoxide alarm, loud cracking right now, a floor, ceiling or wall giving way right now (no booking until it is safe), live wires hanging down, flooding up to the outlets (booking goes on, that area left out). A crack, a sloping floor or a sticking door is the everyday reason to book and is NOT a stop word. The danger-first call (B3-11, B3-18) uses water up to the outlets, so the two steps read as one conversation.
Settings: arrive a set start (8:00am and 1:00pm), cutoff 6pm the day before; booking choices limited to a set time (timing settime, times setstart). Nothing is sent now: S2-30's Yes branch and every sent-now branch are off, and the joined text says no work is sent now.
Rename pairs: only the inspector's pairs that match the frozen master were kept (about 140 A, 200 B; the rest matched nothing) and re-worded for engineering; addresses and license numbers are made-up (EX-1042 style). The master's 'Leak repair' sign-up row now reads 'Large property evaluation' (priced at the visit by size; the fee never depends on what is found).
Own steps (same ids as the parent): B6-x01 (Alex gets a link to forward to whoever sets up access) and B7-x02 (the access is set up on the link). Words ops: the report-later branch (B10-25, B10-19, B10-26), the walk-through (B8-39), check-in by the lockbox (B8-01 to B8-12, B8-17, B8-45, B8-52), the agreement (B5-34 to B5-36) and the trip-fee edges.
Dropped from the parent: its money words per path, its pay-at-closing path, its quoted-money reminders. For the verifier: the walk-through stays the parent's design (Alex meets the engineer near the end; a lockbox lets the engineer in); a reviewer may prefer a no-walk-through variant for engineers who never meet the client.
